subject: This week's strangest signals: On curiosity, F-150 owner complaints, Model Y owner complaints
preheader: On curiosity for On Holding: +94% (38,941 → 75,637) vs the 28 days before. Plus 4 more offbeat moves, explained in plain English.

picks.plain: More people are looking up On than in recent weeks.
picks.what: How many people look up “On (company)” on Wikipedia each day.
picks.why: On is a fast-growing brand, and its growth depends on more people discovering its shoes.

picks.plain: Complaints have eased versus the prior few months.
picks.what: Complaints F-150 owners file with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
picks.why: The F-Series is Ford's profit machine, and Ford has led the industry in recalls.

picks.plain: Complaints are climbing faster than the prior few months.
picks.what: Complaints Model Y owners file with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the federal auto-safety regulator.
picks.why: The Model Y is Tesla's best-selling car.

picks.basis: vs the same period last year
picks.plain: The drug's footprint is growing versus a year ago.
picks.what: Reports of side effects filed with the FDA that mention tirzepatide, Lilly's blockbuster weight-loss and diabetes drug.
picks.why: More patients means more reports, so the trend is a rough, unusual proxy for how fast use is growing.

picks.plain: Interest in iPhones is cooling off compared with recent weeks.
picks.what: How many people look up “iPhone” on Wikipedia each day.
picks.why: iPhones are roughly half of Apple's revenue.

story.title: On curiosity rose 94% (38,941 → 75,637) (vs the 28 days before)
paragraphs: How many people look up “On (company)” on Wikipedia each day. It is a free, public stand-in for search interest: when curiosity spikes, pageviews usually spike too.

Why it might matter for On Holding: on is a fast-growing brand, and its growth depends on more people discovering its shoes. Rising curiosity is an early hint of new customers; a fade suggests the buzz is cooling.
What it shows now: more people are looking up On than in recent weeks. We read that as a notable tailwind for On Holding, which is a clue, not a forecast.

trackLine: In our backtest (Jan 2023–Oct 2026), the stock moved the way the lean pointed over the next month 49.3% of the time (522 of 1058). Beat the market (did it do better than the S&P 500 over the same month, the tougher test): 49% (515 of 1050). That's about a coin flip, so treat these as conversation starters, not predictions.
